\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\title{Edge Stability in a Medium-Sized Tokamak During Current Ramps}
\author{K. Hagen and M. Petrov}
\date{March 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Introduction}
Controlled fusion requires a plasma that remains stable
while the discharge is driven toward its operating point.
The current ramp phase is particularly delicate
because the safety factor profile evolves quickly
and the edge pressure gradient can cross stability boundaries.
We analyse a database of ramp discharges from a medium-sized tokamak
to identify which actuators keep the edge below the peeling-ballooning limit.

\section{Database}
The database covers one hundred and forty ramp discharges
from the last two experimental campaigns.
Each discharge is labelled by its actuator trajectory,
and failed ramps are labelled by the time of the first edge crash.
Roughly a third of the discharges develop edge localised modes
before the flat top is reached.

\section{Plasma Equilibrium}
The axisymmetric equilibrium is reconstructed from magnetic measurements
and from the kinetic pressure profile.
The poloidal beta of the reconstructed equilibria is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ of the volume averaged
value used in the simplified scaling,
which matters for the stability boundary.

Fuel for these discharges is the standard D & T mixture with trace helium ash,
and the edge fuelling is dominated by gas puffing from the midplane valves.

The pressure gradient is limited by the edge bootstrap current,
and throughout the ramp the ratio $\beta stays below the Troyon limit
for every reconstructed time slice.

Reconstructions are computed every five milliseconds
and interpolated onto a common grid for the stability analysis.
The reconstruction residuals are small compared with the measurement noise,
so the equilibria are treated as exact in the stability step.

\section{Diagnostics}
The main diagnostics used in this study are:
\begin{itemize}
\item a Thomson scattering system covering the edge pedestal;
\item a magnetic probe array on the outboard midplane;
\item a fast camera viewing the divertor leg.
\section{Stability Boundaries}
The peeling-ballooning boundary is computed with an ideal MHD code
using the reconstructed equilibria as input.
Discharges that cross the boundary during the ramp
develop edge localised modes within two milliseconds of the crossing,
which validates the boundary calculation.
The boundary is most sensitive to the edge current density,
and less so to the details of the pressure profile near the separatrix.

\section{Transport Modelling}
Turbulent transport between crashes is modelled with a gyrofluid code.
The simulations use experimental profiles and flows,
and the predicted heat flux is compared with power balance.
\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.6\textwidth]{figures/te_profile_evolution.pdf}
\caption{Evolution of the edge temperature profile during the ramp.}
\end{figure}
The simulated heat flux matches the power balance estimate
within the experimental uncertainty for most of the ramp.
Agreement degrades briefly after each edge crash,
when the profiles are furthest from the assumed quasi-steady state.

\section{Actuator Response}
Increasing the gas puff rate early in the ramp
moves the pedestal away from the boundary
at the cost of a lower confinement factor.
Shaping the plasma with a higher triangularity
achieves a similar margin without the confinement penalty,
and the two actuators combine favourably.
The response time of the margin to a shaping change
is about fifty milliseconds in our database,
which sets the latency budget for any feedback scheme.

\section{Toward Feedback Control}
A simple supervisor monitors the distance to the boundary
and adjusts the fuelling waveform in real time.
In a shadow-mode trial the supervisor would have prevented
roughly two thirds of the observed edge crashes
without violating the density limit.

\section{Conclusion}
Edge stability during the current ramp can be maintained
with a combination of early fuelling and higher triangularity.
The scaling derived here is being integrated
into the discharge supervision system of the device,
and a closed-loop demonstration is planned for the next campaign.
\end{document}
